definitions.explanation: The resistance or texture felt when biting into food; the satisfying sensation of chewing.
Something that provides resistance or challenge, making it worthwhile.

examples.japanese: この{野菜|やさい}は{歯応|はごた}えがある。
examples.english: These vegetables have a nice crunch.

examples.japanese: アルデンテのパスタは{歯応|はごた}えがいい。
examples.english: Al dente pasta has a good bite.

examples.japanese: {歯応|はごた}えのある{相手|あいて}と{対戦|たいせん}したい。
examples.english: I want to compete against a challenging opponent.

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
{歯|は} (tooth) + {応|こた}え (response) → response to teeth = chewiness

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{歯応|はごた}えがある (has a good bite/is crunchy)
・{歯応|はごた}えがいい (has a nice texture)
・{歯応|はごた}えのある (chewy, crunchy; challenging)

RELATED ～{応|ごた}え WORDS:
・{読|よ}み{応|ごた}え (worth reading)
・{見応|みごた}え (worth seeing)
・{聞|き}き{応|ごた}え (worth listening to)
・{食|く}い{応|ごた}え (filling, satisfying to eat)

USAGE NOTE:
The figurative sense (sense 2) is common in competitive contexts, describing opponents or tasks that provide satisfying resistance.
